item.title: Sustainable Strategic Knowledge Management in the Era of AI
item.content:encoded:
Organizations face increasing complexity from shifting geopolitical, economic, and technological conditions, requiring strategic approaches to knowledge management for sustainability. The integration of knowledge management with AI offers potential benefits for problem-solving and decision-making, yet presents challenges that require responsible and ethical implementation. This special issue examines how organizations can leverage strategic knowledge management to balance the opportunities and risks of AI while maintaining sustainability across their operations.

The call seeks contributions exploring how organizations can effectively manage both human knowledge and AI-generated intelligent knowledge, addressing issues such as knowledge overload, loss, and duplication. It emphasizes the importance of codification and personalization strategies that align with organizational values and objectives. The special issue invites researchers to examine how sustainable strategic knowledge management enables organizations to adapt to rapidly changing environments while achieving economic, social, and environmental goals.

Appel publié par Journal of Strategy and Management. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Knowledge management processes and sustainability in organizations
  • Human-AI synergy and responsible AI use in knowledge systems
  • Strategic knowledge management for organizational decision-making and problem-solving
  • Managing explicit and tacit knowledge in digital environments
  • Knowledge codification and personalization approaches
  • Addressing knowledge overload from AI, cloud computing, and big data
  • Sustainable knowledge-based organizations and resource optimization
  • AI's impact on critical knowledge management processes
  • Ethical and mission-aligned strategic knowledge for financial, social, and ecological benefits
  • Knowledge management in complex organizational environments and geopolitical uncertainty

Timeline

  • January 8, 2026: Opening date for manuscripts submissions
  • October 31, 2026: Closing date for manuscripts submission

item.title: The role of social capital in knowledge management
item.content:encoded:
This special issue explores the interconnection between social capital and knowledge management in organizations. Social capital—networks of relationships, trust, and shared norms—facilitates knowledge exchange and integration, enhancing intellectual capital development and organizational competitiveness across sectors including technology, finance, healthcare, and creative industries.

The call addresses critical research gaps including the lack of general theory explaining how social capital translates to intellectual capital across different contexts, inconsistent measurement approaches, and limited longitudinal studies. It seeks contributions examining how social capital functions as a mediating mechanism in digital environments, how it evolves over time, and how cultural and technological factors influence these dynamics.

The special issue invites empirical and theoretical research from academics and practitioners investigating social capital's role in knowledge creation, innovation outcomes, and competitive advantage, with particular attention to measurement frameworks, trust mechanisms, and organizational structures that enable effective knowledge management.

Appel publié par VINE Journal of Information and Knowledge Management Systems. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • How does social capital translate into intellectual capital across different organizational contexts?
  • In what ways does social capital act as a mediator of knowledge management in digital and dynamic environments?
  • How can social capital in knowledge management be measured? To what extent do trust, networks, and norms function as distinct versus overlapping dimensions of social capital?
  • How does social capital evolve over time, and what are its long-term effects on knowledge creation and sharing?
  • How do individual employee networks aggregate to create firm-level intellectual capital?
  • How is social capital value disclosed?
  • How do national cultures influence the relationship between social capital and knowledge management?
  • In what ways do organizational structures influence the effectiveness of social capital in enabling knowledge management?
  • How do emerging technologies impact the development and role of social capital in knowledge management?
  • What role does trust play in knowledge sharing and knowledge application processes?
  • How can organizations foster trust to strengthen social capital in virtual and hybrid workplaces?
  • How does social capital-driven knowledge management contribute to organizational innovation?
  • What is the relationship between social capital, knowledge management, and competitive advantage in dynamic markets?

Timeline

  • April 1, 2026: Opening date for manuscript submissions
  • October 31, 2026: Closing date for manuscript submissions

item.title: Action Learning in Asia
item.content:encoded:
George Boak, York St John University

Wooyong Eom, Keimyung University

Sanghyeok Park, Gyeongsang National University

Christine Abbott, Centre for Action Learning

This special issue invites contributions exploring action learning across Asia. While previous journal issues have featured individual papers on action learning in various Asian countries, this collection seeks to expand representation to underrepresented regions throughout the continent.

The editors are particularly interested in how cultural contexts shape action learning approaches. Submissions should examine whether distinctive characteristics emerge in action learning design and facilitation across different cultural settings, and how cultural factors influence both the aims and processes of action learning.

The issue welcomes empirical studies, conceptual papers, and practitioner accounts that contribute to understanding action learning theory and practice in Asian contexts. Authors are encouraged to consult with editors before submitting full papers.

Appel publié par Action Learning: Research and Practice. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Action learning practices and theory in Asian countries including South Korea, China, Japan, the Philippines, Thailand, Singapore, Taiwan, Turkey, Nepal, India and Pakistan
  • Cultural influences on action learning design, aims and processes
  • Distinctive characteristics of action learning facilitation in different cultural environments
  • Empirical and conceptual explorations of action learning
  • Practitioner accounts and personal experiences of action learning

Timeline

  • October 1, 2026: Manuscript deadline

item.title: AI Literacy at Work: Implications for Human Resource Management
item.content:encoded:
Maarten Renkema, University of Twente

Laura Lamers, University of Twente

Christoph Lutz, BI Norwegian Business School

Anna B. Holm, Aarhus University

Organizations are rapidly adopting AI technologies, but this creates significant challenges including algorithmic bias and opacity. AI literacy—the knowledge, skills, and attitudes enabling individuals to engage effectively and critically with AI—has become essential for competitive survival and is now mandated by the EU's AI Act. However, research on AI literacy remains focused primarily on educational contexts and individual learners, leaving organizational and HRM perspectives largely unexplored.

This special issue seeks to advance theoretical understanding of AI literacy as an organizational phenomenon rather than merely an individual competency. The editors invite contributions that move beyond both naive enthusiasm and dismissive skepticism, instead adopting critically engaged perspectives grounded in empirical evidence. Contributions should examine AI literacy across multiple organizational levels—individual, team, and organizational—and explore how HRM can facilitate its development and implications for HR functions and practices.

Appel publié par The International Journal of Human Resource Management. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Implications of AI literacy for core HRM functions including recruitment, selection, learning and development, performance management, and employee well-being
  • Organizational AI literacy: design, implementation, and governance of HRM activities
  • Emergence mechanisms through which individual AI literacy becomes collective organizational capability
  • Relationship between organizational AI literacy and adjacent constructs such as organizational AI readiness
  • Competition for AI talent and inequality implications
  • Team design and composition to enable and develop AI literacy
  • HRM and HRD practices supporting AI-literate teams including workforce planning, staffing, job design, and training
  • Levels and combinations of AI literacy needed across different teams and roles
  • Manifestation of AI literacy in everyday work practices
  • Technical, ethical and practical dimensions of AI literacy in AI-mediated recruitment
  • AI literacy's influence on employees' AI overreliance and fairness perceptions
  • AI literacy of HR professionals and its influence on adoption of AI tools

item.title: Knowledge Management despite Resource and Institutional limitations: Advancing Innovation, Resilience, and Organizational Learning
item.content:encoded:
Guillermo Antonio Dávila, Universidad de Lima

Susanne Durst, Bangkok University

Organizations in resource-constrained and institutionally weak contexts face significant challenges in maintaining competitiveness and innovation amid political uncertainty and technological change. This special issue addresses the underexamined role of knowledge management in enabling these organizations—including SMEs, NGOs, and entities in developing regions—to overcome financial constraints, limited technological access, and skilled workforce shortages.

Knowledge management has demonstrated capacity to enhance innovation, strengthen organizational resilience, and foster learning even under severe resource limitations. While empirical evidence from emerging economies supports these benefits, research remains concentrated on stable, well-developed environments, leaving underrepresented contexts insufficiently studied despite their numerical significance and potential for theoretical contribution.

Appel publié par Knowledge Management Research & Practice. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • KM as an enabler of organizational performance under conditions of resource scarcity
  • Knowledge risk management as crucial function in environments characterized by internal and external constraints
  • KM in underrepresented organisational settings, including SMEs, family businesses, informal organisations, low-technology firms, social organisations or geographically isolated regions
  • Organisational learning processes in contexts characterised by institutional and resource constraints
  • The role of KM in strengthening organisational resilience during internal and external crises and disruptions
  • Necessary conditions and bottlenecks for organizational development empowered by KM
  • The interplay between artificial intelligence and KM in overcoming organisational and institutional constraints
  • The role of institutional ecosystems and inter-organisational networks in enhancing the effectiveness of KM
  • Novel methodological approaches for studying KM in constrained and underrepresented contexts

Timeline

  • March 15, 2027: Manuscript deadline
